claims.statement: Poland's accessibility law applying the European Accessibility Act took effect on 28 June 2025, changing requirements for covered products and services.
Covered digital businesses currently pay developers, auditors, or agencies to identify and remediate accessibility defects; the average Polish spend is unknown.
The founder can own a testing workflow and evidence format without privileged data, but access to production systems requires customer contracts not currently held.

commercial_mechanics.budget_owner: Digital-product owner, compliance lead, or e-commerce manager
commercial_mechanics.bundling_resistance: Web agencies and testing suites bundle scans; fixed-scope Polish evidence packs and verified remediation distinguish the offer
commercial_mechanics.customer_relationship_owner: Unknown today; proposed direct contracts with Polish digital-service SMEs
commercial_mechanics.distribution_origin: Automated website screening, agency referrals, and targeted outbound

fully_loaded_economics.acquisition_cost: Assumption: 1,500-5,000 PLN per client; unknown until outreach
fully_loaded_economics.contribution_margin: Assumption: 55-70% after specialist QA and remediation subcontracting
fully_loaded_economics.delivery_and_support_costs: Assumption: 20-60 hours per sprint depending on scope
fully_loaded_economics.overhead_and_compliance: Accessibility legal review and professional liability; exact cost unknown
fully_loaded_economics.revenue_basis: Fixed audit/remediation sprint plus quarterly monitoring
fully_loaded_economics.variable_costs: Automated scanning, manual assistive-technology testing, and developer time

commercial_mechanics.likely_incumbent_response: Agencies package compliance into maintenance retainers
commercial_mechanics.paid_event_or_measurable_loss: Current audit and developer hours spent finding, documenting, and fixing inaccessible journeys after the law became applicable
commercial_mechanics.payer: Covered e-commerce, banking, transport, communications, or digital-service SME
commercial_mechanics.purchase_trigger: Complaint, procurement questionnaire, product launch, or overdue post-law compliance review
commercial_mechanics.renewal_event: Quarterly regression test or major release

contrary_evidence: Automated scanners are inexpensive and widely available.
Not every SME or service falls within scope, and exemptions require legal screening.

critical_control_point.acquisition_instrument: Ownership of a reusable testing harness plus proposed customer service agreement for authenticated journey access
critical_control_point.counterparty_refusal_fallback: Audit public unauthenticated journeys and provide a limited findings report
critical_control_point.current_owner: Founder can create and own the testing harness; customers own applications and authenticated access
critical_control_point.customer_relationship_owner: Unknown today; proposed direct contracts with Polish digital-service SMEs
critical_control_point.duration: Testing harness ownership is indefinite; customer access duration unknown
critical_control_point.founder_access_description: Founder can independently build the harness using public standards and open tooling; no employer resources are needed
critical_control_point.launch_controller: Prospective business controls the harness; customer controls remediation deployment
critical_control_point.renewal: Not applicable to owned harness; customer monitoring contracts proposed quarterly
critical_control_point.subject: Accessibility testing harness and evidence-pack generator

economics.acquisition_route: Scan 100 public sites, sell five fixed-scope audits, subcontract manual testing, then convert successful clients to monitoring
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Assumption: productization to 1,000 monitored properties at 500 PLN monthly yields 6m PLN ARR; a 20% owner-earnings profile or recurring equity value could exceed 5m PLN in 5-8 years. Conversion and retention are unknown.
economics.founder_time: 15-25 hours weekly; manual specialist testing must be scheduled or subcontracted
economics.gross_margin_basis: Fees less scanner infrastructure, manual QA, and remediation subcontractors
economics.payback: Assumption: under 3 months if a 2,500 PLN acquisition cost leads to a 10,000 PLN sprint at 60% contribution
economics.pricing: Assumption: 6,000-25,000 PLN sprint and 300-1,500 PLN monthly monitoring

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Reusable Polish-language evidence templates and defect-to-fix benchmark data
fingerprint.customer: Polish SMEs operating covered digital consumer services
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Fixed-scope audit/remediation sprint with monitoring subscription
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Product owner pays for audit and developer remediation after accessibility defects are found
fingerprint.problem_trigger: Accessibility requirements became applicable to covered services

founder_fit: AI-assisted testing and report generation fit the founder's technical leverage.
Fixed-scope delivery can be run part-time.
risks: Legal scope determinations require qualified review.

structural_signature.commercial_model_descriptor: fixed scope accessibility proof and remediation sprint

thesis: Post-effective-date compliance creates demand for a bounded Polish accessibility evidence sprint that sits between cheap scanners and expensive consultancies.
title: Accessibility Proof Sprint for Polish SMEs
uncertainties: Availability and cost of manual testers are unknown.
